#Preamble
We have a pretty detailed MN filtering script as we have extensive knowledge of the data. First we read in the Minnesota data. The next section manipulates the MN data to make filtering easier, including filtering out records with flags, choosing sampling methods, and filtering effort based on lake size. 

#Library
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
```

#Data
```{r}
#fish data
mn_data <- open_dataset(sources = file.path("G:",
                                            "Shared drives",
                                            "Hansen Lab",
                                            "RESEARCH PROJECTS",
                                            "Fish Survey Data",
                                            "Parquet files",
                                            "mn_update"))
glimpse(mn_data)

#area data for filtering
area <- read_csv(file.path("G:",
                           "Shared drives",
                           "Hansen Lab",
                           "RESEARCH PROJECTS",
                           "Fish Survey Data",
                           "manuscript_products",
                           "abundance",
                           "data",
                           "input",
                           "mn_lake_list.csv")) %>%
  select(DOW, LAKE_AREA_DOW_ACRES) %>%
  mutate(DOW = as.integer(DOW)) %>% 
  rename(lake_id = DOW,
         lake_area = LAKE_AREA_DOW_ACRES)

#adding a few lakes that don't show
#data pulled from lake finder
adds <- data.frame(
  lake_id = as.integer(c("56038800", 
                         "55006400", 
                         "76014601", 
                         "76014602",
                         "73076800",
                         "69148100",
                         "69096700",
                         "69027300",
                         "7016600")),
  lake_area = c(1288, 20, 467, 218, 9, 1, 2, 15, 0)
)
area <- bind_rows(area, adds) %>% 
  mutate(lake_id = as.character(lake_id))
rm(adds)  
```

#data filters for MN
This chunk must be run before filtering as it applied necessary data manipulations prior to filtering. Working with mn data directly to select sampling methods, survey types, area filters, effort filters etc. In Minnesota, we are only interested in the standard surveys, passive gears where species are not "targeted" so we will not worry about the target species column
```{r}
#1.) effort flags - lets just apply an all encompassing effort flag to any survey flagged within the data base for effort. Effort flags appear to have been applied at the obs level, with a small subset of TEIs where some fish have an effort flag but some do not. That doesn't really make sense, so we will apply a flag to all records in a tei that have at least one record with an effort level flag
mn_data %>% 
  distinct(cpue_invalid, flag) %>%
  collect() %>% 
  arrange(cpue_invalid) %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

mn_data %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, cpue_invalid) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  group_by(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  filter(n >1)
#the only total effort ident that has more than one cpue invalid flag is NA total effort ident and we wont have to worry about it

mn_data %>% 
  filter(is.na(total_effort_ident) & cpue_invalid == "n") %>% 
  group_by(is.na(total_effort_1)) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  collect()
#all places where there shows a vaild cpue survey, there is NA effort 

#2.) picking the standard sampling methods
mn_data %>% 
  distinct(sampling_method_simple,
           sampling_method,
           sampling_method_2) %>%
  collect() %>% 
  arrange(sampling_method_simple, sampling_method) %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))
#we have standard gill nets but there does not appear to be a standard trap net listed

mn_data %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, sampling_method, sampling_method_2) %>% 
  filter(sampling_method == "trap_net") %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method_2) %>%
  count() %>% 
  collect()
#we see here that the most used and standard trap net is the 0.75 inch double frame

#lets create a call so that this trap net gets called standard for the inclusion table
mn_data %>% 
  mutate(sampling_method = case_when(sampling_method_2 == "trap_net; 0.75-in-mesh net; double-frame net" ~ "trap_net_standard",
         TRUE ~ sampling_method)) %>% 
  filter(sampling_method_simple == "frame_net") %>% 
  distinct(sampling_method, sampling_method_2) %>% 
  collect()

mn_data <- mn_data %>% 
  mutate(sampling_method = case_when(sampling_method_2 == "trap_net; 0.75-in-mesh net; double-frame net" ~ "trap_net_standard",
         TRUE ~ sampling_method))

mn_data %>% 
  filter(sampling_method_simple == "frame_net") %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method, sampling_method_2) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  collect()

#3.) Picking the survey types 
mn_data %>% 
  distinct(survey_type) %>% 
  collect()

mn_data %>% 
  mutate(survey_type_filter = case_when(survey_type %in% c("HISTORICAL",
                                                 "Large Lake Survey", 
                                                 "Population Assessment",
                                                 "Standard Survey",
                                                 "Initial Survey",
                                                 "Re-Survey") ~ "y", 
                              TRUE ~ "n")) %>% 
  distinct(survey_type, survey_type_filter) %>% 
  arrange(survey_type_filter, survey_type) %>% 
  collect()

#4.) lake area - first we need to grab the lake areas
mn_data %>% 
  left_join(area) %>% 
  mutate(area_group = case_when(lake_area < 100 ~ "<100",
                                lake_area >= 100 & lake_area <= 300 ~ "100-300",
                                lake_area >= 301 & lake_area <= 600 ~ "301-600",
                                lake_area >= 601 & lake_area <= 1500 ~ "601-1500",
                                lake_area >= 1501 ~ "1501+",
                                TRUE ~ "NA")) %>% 
  group_by(area_group) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  collect()

mn_data <- mn_data %>% 
  #adding a lake area for filtering here 
  left_join(area) %>% 
  mutate(area_group = case_when(lake_area < 100 ~ "<100",
                                lake_area >= 100 & lake_area <= 300 ~ "100-300",
                                lake_area >= 301 & lake_area <= 600 ~ "301-600",
                                lake_area >= 601 & lake_area <= 1500 ~ "601-1500",
                                lake_area >= 1501 ~ "1501+",
                                TRUE ~ "NA")) 
mn_data %>% 
  group_by(is.na(area_group)) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  collect()
rm(area)


#5.) dates
mn_data %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident) %>% 
  collect()

mn_data %>% 
  filter(sampling_method == "angling_ice_fishing") %>% 
  distinct(lake_name, year, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident) %>% 
  collect()

mn_data %>% 
  filter(lake_name == "Leech" & year %in% c(2015, 2018)) %>% 
  distinct(year, sampling_method, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

mn_data %>% 
  filter(lake_name == "Leech" & year %in% c(2021, 2022)) %>% 
  distinct(year, sampling_method, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

mn_data %>% 
  filter(lake_name == "Leech" & !is.na(total_effort_ident)) %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, survey_type, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident, year, month) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  arrange(year) %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

mn_data %>% 
  filter(lake_name == "Leech" & !is.na(total_effort_ident)) %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, survey_type, date_survey, date_total_effort_ident, year, month, sampling_method) %>% 
  collect() %>% 
  arrange(year) %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))
```


General structure for each filtering chunks:
1. gather the filter tables (survey level and fish level)
2. filter for "good surveys"
3. gather fish data from the good surveys
4. calculate cpue - ensuring you are counting fish of the correct parameters
   -if fish level counting within certain parameters is desired (bin lengths) apply that here
5. check survey level filtering
6. check filtering post gathering fish
7. check cpue generation
8. remove large individual fish object to save memory 

#walleye filtering
```{r}
#filters for metric and selects columns needed for survey filtering
filter_table_effort <- read_csv(file.path("G:",
                                          "Shared drives",
                                          "Hansen Lab",
                                          "RESEARCH PROJECTS",
                                          "Fish Survey Data",
                                          "manuscript_products",
                                          "abundance",
                                          "data",
                                          "input",
                                          "cpue_inclusion_table.csv")) %>% 
  filter(metric == "adult_abundance" & state == "Minnesota" & species_1 == "walleye") %>% 
  select(-metric,
         -species_1,
         -water_temp_min,
         -water_temp_max,
         -survey_type)

good_surveys <- mn_data %>%
  # #picking standard trap net gear - this is already done for gill nets but we need to make sure we grab standard trap nets
  # #filter for correct survey type
  mutate(survey_type_filter = case_when(survey_type %in% c("HISTORICAL",
                                                 "Large Lake Survey",
                                                 "Population Assessment",
                                                 "Standard Survey",
                                                 "Initial Survey",
                                                 "Re-Survey") ~ "y",
                              TRUE ~ "n")) %>%
  right_join(filter_table_effort, by = c("state",
                                        "sampling_method",
                                        "area_group")) %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type,
           survey_type_filter,
           cpue_invalid)  %>%
  filter(total_effort_1 >= effort_min,
         total_effort_1 <= effort_max,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) >= month_min,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) <= month_max,
         survey_type_filter == "y",
         cpue_invalid == "n") %>%
  collect() 

#gather fish from the surveys deemed good for abundance of the given species
adult_walleye <- mn_data %>% 
  #filter the data for surveys that were good for species abundance
  right_join(good_surveys) %>% 
  collect() 

#create cpue for species of interest
adult_walleye_cpue <- adult_walleye %>% 
  #grouping by survey level parameters to get survey level counts
  group_by(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  #counts fish of a particular species in a survey 
  mutate(count = sum(species_1 == 'walleye')) %>% 
  #surveys that did not catch fish (species column is na) return a catch of 0
  mutate(count = case_when(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE" ~ 0,
                           TRUE ~ count)) %>% 
  #generates cpue from counts and efforts associated with that survey count
  mutate(cpue = count/total_effort_1) %>%
  #collapse data into survey level cpue (also works as a select function)
  distinct(total_effort_ident,
           .keep_all = T) 

adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  filter(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE") %>% 
  distinct(lake_id, year, sampling_method)

#checking filtering
#survey level checks
#min effort by grouping
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(area_group) %>% 
  summarise(min_effort = min(total_effort_1),
            n = n())

#checks after collecting all fish data
#is each sampling method correct for the filter?
adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

adult_walleye %>% 
  group_by(survey_type, sampling_method, survey_type_filter) %>% 
  count()

adult_walleye %>% 
  group_by(flag) %>% 
  count()

#do I retain all of the good surveys? - rows here should match good surveys 
adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           survey_type,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  glimpse()

#there are a handful of surveys that have multiple efforts within a total effort ident
#this causes the good surveys to look bigger than the cpue total but ensure we get all fish records 
adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  glimpse()

adult_walleye %>% 
  group_by(total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  group_by(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  filter(n > 1)

adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           #total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type_filter) %>% 
  glimpse()

adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type_filter) %>% 
  group_by(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type_filter) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  filter(n >1)

#85 nothing caught surveys, but they were removed from the cpe product
adult_walleye %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  group_by(total_effort_nothing_caught) %>% 
  count()

#checks after calculating cpue

#range of cpues?
adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min = min(cpue), max = max(cpue))

#any na cpue?
adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  filter(is.na(cpue))

#surveys that have nothing caught?
adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  filter(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE") %>% 
  group_by(lake_name, survey_type, sampling_method, total_effort_1, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_nothing_caught, cpue) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(cpue)) +
  facet_wrap(~sampling_method, scales = "free")

#here is an example of a lake-year-method that had more than one tei, we can see that we capture the total effort ident we want based on its survey type
mn_data %>% 
  filter(lake_id == "11014700" & year == 1997 & sampling_method == "gill_net_standard") %>% 
  group_by(survey_type) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  collect()

adult_walleye %>% 
  filter(lake_id == "11014700" & year == 1997 & sampling_method == "gill_net_standard") %>% 
  group_by(survey_type) %>% 
  count()

#here are examples of there being two total effort idents, different by survey_type on the same day
multi <- adult_walleye %>% 
  group_by(lake_id, sampling_method, year) %>% 
  summarise(n_tei = n_distinct(total_effort_ident)) %>% 
  filter(n_tei >1)

check <- adult_walleye %>% 
  semi_join(multi, by = c("lake_id", "sampling_method", "year")) %>% 
  group_by(lake_id, survey_type, year, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_1, sampling_method, date_survey, total_effort_ident) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  arrange(lake_id, survey_type, year, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_1)
#all lake-gear-year duplicates have valid splits (varying total efforts, survey type, or date)
rm(multi, check)

adult_walleye_cpue %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  count()

#removes individual fish object to save memory
rm(adult_walleye)
```

#black crappie filtering
```{r}
#filters for metric and selects columns needed for survey filtering
filter_table_effort <- read_csv(file.path("G:",
                                          "Shared drives",
                                          "Hansen Lab",
                                          "RESEARCH PROJECTS",
                                          "Fish Survey Data",
                                          "manuscript_products",
                                          "abundance",
                                          "data",
                                          "input",
                                          "cpue_inclusion_table.csv")) %>% 
  filter(metric == "adult_abundance" & state == "Minnesota" & species_1 == "black_crappie") %>% 
  select(-metric,
         -species_1,
         -water_temp_min,
         -water_temp_max,
         -survey_type)

#filters for surveys that are good measures of abundance for given fish species
#first, merge the filter table with the data - selects for non-numeric parameters important for abundance 
#second, collapse the data into survey level
#third, filter the surveys based on numeric values 
good_surveys <- mn_data %>%
  #filter for correct survey_type
  mutate(survey_type_filter = case_when(survey_type %in% c("HISTORICAL", 
                                                 "Large Lake Survey", 
                                                 "Population Assessment",
                                                 "Standard Survey",
                                                 "Initial Survey",
                                                 "Re-Survey") ~ "y", 
                              TRUE ~ "n")) %>% 
  right_join(filter_table_effort, by = c("state",
                                        "sampling_method",
                                        "area_group")) %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type_filter,
           cpue_invalid) %>% 
  filter(total_effort_1 >= effort_min,
         total_effort_1 <= effort_max,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) >= month_min,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) <= month_max,
         survey_type_filter == "y",
         cpue_invalid == "n") %>% 
  collect() 

#gather fish from the surveys deemed good for abundance of the given species
adult_black_crappie <- mn_data %>% 
  #filter the data for surveys that were good for species abundance
  right_join(good_surveys) %>% 
  collect() 

#create cpue for species of interest
adult_black_crappie_cpue <- adult_black_crappie %>% 
  #grouping by survey level parameters to get survey level counts
  group_by(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  #counts fish of a particular species in a survey 
  mutate(count = sum(species_1 == 'black_crappie')) %>% 
  #surveys that did not catch fish (species column is na) return a catch of 0
  mutate(count = case_when(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE" ~ 0,
                           TRUE ~ count)) %>% 
  #generates cpue from counts and efforts associated with that survey count
  mutate(cpue = count/total_effort_1) %>%
  #collapse data into survey level cpue (also works as a select function)
  distinct(total_effort_ident,
           .keep_all = T) 


#checking filtering

#survey level checks
#month range
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

#min effort by grouping
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(area_group, sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min_effort = min(total_effort_1),
            n = n())

#checks after collecting all fish data
#is each sampling method correct for the filter?
adult_black_crappie %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

adult_black_crappie %>% 
  group_by(survey_type, sampling_method, survey_type_filter) %>% 
  count()

adult_black_crappie %>% 
  group_by(flag) %>% 
  count()

#do I retain all of the good surveys? - rows here should match good surveys 
adult_black_crappie %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  glimpse()

#do we have the number of surveys as expected in good surveys?
adult_black_crappie %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  glimpse()

adult_black_crappie %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           #total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1)  

adult_black_crappie %>% 
  group_by(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  summarise(n_TEIs = n_distinct(total_effort_ident),
            n_tyes = n_distinct(survey_type)) %>% 
  filter(n_TEIs > 1)



#checks after calculating cpue
#range of cpues?
adult_black_crappie_cpue %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min = min(cpue), max = max(cpue))

#any na cpue?
adult_black_crappie_cpue %>% 
  filter(is.na(cpue))

#surveys that have nothing caught?
adult_black_crappie_cpue %>% 
  filter(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE") %>% 
  group_by(lake_name, survey_type, sampling_method, total_effort_1, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_nothing_caught, cpue) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

adult_black_crappie_cpue %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(cpue)) +
  facet_wrap(~sampling_method, scales = "free")



#removes individual fish object to save memory
rm(adult_black_crappie)
```

```{r}
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)),

  distinct(lake_id,
```

#largemouth filtering
```{r}
#filters for metric and selects columns needed for survey filtering
filter_table_effort <- read_csv(file.path("G:",
                                          "Shared drives",
                                          "Hansen Lab",
                                          "RESEARCH PROJECTS",
                                          "Fish Survey Data",
                                          "manuscript_products",
                                          "abundance",
                                          "data",
                                          "input",
                                          "cpue_inclusion_table.csv")) %>% 
  filter(metric == "adult_abundance" & state == "Minnesota" & species_1 == "largemouth_bass") %>% 
  select(-metric,
         -species_1,
         -water_temp_min,
         -water_temp_max,
         -survey_type)

#filters for surveys that are good measures of abundance for given fish species
#first, merge the filter table with the data - selects for non-numeric parameters important for abundance 
#second, collapse the data into survey level
#third, filter the surveys based on numeric values 
good_surveys <- mn_data %>%
  #filter for correct survey_type
  mutate(survey_type_filter = case_when(survey_type %in% c("HISTORICAL", 
                                                 "Large Lake Survey", 
                                                 "Population Assessment",
                                                 "Standard Survey",
                                                 "Initial Survey",
                                                 "Re-Survey") ~ "y", 
                              TRUE ~ "n")) %>% 
  right_join(filter_table_effort, by = c("state",
                                        "sampling_method",
                                        "area_group")) %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_1,
           area_group,
           effort_min,
           effort_max,
           month_min,
           month_max,
           survey_type_filter,
           cpue_invalid) %>% 
  filter(total_effort_1 >= effort_min,
         total_effort_1 <= effort_max,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) >= month_min,
         month(date_total_effort_ident) <= month_max,
         survey_type_filter == "y",
         cpue_invalid == "n") %>% 
  collect() 

#gather fish from the surveys deemed good for abundance of the given species
adult_largemouth_bass <- mn_data %>% 
  #filter the data for surveys that were good for species abundance
  right_join(good_surveys) %>% 
  collect() 

#create cpue for species of interest
adult_largemouth_bass_cpue <- adult_largemouth_bass %>% 
  #grouping by survey level parameters to get survey level counts
  group_by(total_effort_ident) %>% 
  #counts fish of a particular species in a survey 
  mutate(count = sum(species_1 == 'largemouth_bass')) %>% 
  #surveys that did not catch fish (species column is na) return a catch of 0
  mutate(count = case_when(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE" ~ 0,
                           TRUE ~ count)) %>% 
  #generates cpue from counts and efforts associated with that survey count
  mutate(cpue = count/total_effort_1) %>%
  #collapse data into survey level cpue (also works as a select function)
  distinct(total_effort_ident,
           .keep_all = T)


#checking filtering

#survey level checks

good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

#min effort by grouping
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(area_group, sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min_effort = min(total_effort_1),
            n = n())

#checks after collecting all fish data
#is each sampling method correct for the filter?
adult_largemouth_bass %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

adult_largemouth_bass %>% 
  group_by(survey_type, sampling_method, survey_type_filter) %>% 
  count()

adult_largemouth_bass %>% 
  group_by(flag) %>% 
  count()

#do I retain all of the good surveys? - rows here should match good surveys 
adult_largemouth_bass %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           survey_type,
           sampling_method,

#checks after calculating cpue

#any na cpue?
adult_largemouth_bass_cpue %>% 
  filter(is.na(cpue))

#surveys that have nothing caught?
adult_largemouth_bass_cpue %>% 
  filter(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE") %>% 
  group_by(lake_name, survey_type, sampling_method, total_effort_1, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_nothing_caught, cpue) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

adult_largemouth_bass_cpue %>%
```

```{r}
  mutate(count = sum(species_1 == 'yellow_perch')) %>% 
  #surveys that did not catch fish (species column is na) return a catch of 0
  mutate(count = case_when(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE" ~ 0,
                           TRUE ~ count)) %>% 
  #generates cpue from counts and efforts associated with that survey count
  mutate(cpue = count/total_effort_1) %>%
  #collapse data into survey level cpue (also works as a select function)
  distinct(total_effort_ident,
           .keep_all = T)


#checking filtering

#survey level checks
#month range
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

#min effort by grouping
good_surveys %>% 
  group_by(area_group, sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min_effort = min(total_effort_1),
            n = n())

#checks after collecting all fish data
#is each sampling method correct for the filter?
adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  distinct(total_effort_ident, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min.month = min(month(date_total_effort_ident)), 
            max.month = max(month(date_total_effort_ident)),
            n = n())

adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  group_by(survey_type, sampling_method, survey_type_filter) %>% 
  count()

adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  group_by(flag) %>% 
  count()

#do I retain all of the good surveys? - rows here should match good surveys 
adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           survey_type,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  glimpse()

adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  glimpse()

adult_yellow_perch %>% 
  distinct(lake_id,
           date_total_effort_ident,
           # survey_type,
           # total_effort_ident,
           sampling_method,
           total_effort_1) %>% 
  glimpse()

#checks after calculating cpue
#range of cpues?
adult_yellow_perch_cpue %>% 
  group_by(sampling_method) %>% 
  summarise(min = min(cpue), max = max(cpue))

#any na cpue?
adult_yellow_perch_cpue %>% 
  filter(is.na(cpue))

#surveys that have nothing caught?
adult_yellow_perch_cpue %>% 
  filter(total_effort_nothing_caught == "TRUE") %>% 
  group_by(lake_name, survey_type, sampling_method, total_effort_1, date_total_effort_ident, total_effort_nothing_caught, cpue) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  print(n = nrow(.))

adult_yellow_perch_cpue %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(cpue)) +
  facet_wrap(~sampling_method, scales = "free")

#removes individual fish object to save memory
rm(adult_yellow_perch)
```
